subject: Urgent: EntangleFin reserved-capacity gap causing latency spikes and 5xxs

Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@entanglefin.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Production latency + 5xx surge — reserved capacity not delivering

Marcus —

We're seeing sustained latency increases and a rising rate of 5xx responses across our production endpoints since ~08:30 PST. Error rate gone from ~0.3% to ~4.9% and p95 latency has doubled. Our dashboard shows reserved throughput usage pegged and a backlog of queued tokens. This is impacting payment authorizations; we have queued customer transactions.

We opened a ticket with your support, ticket #RF-7842, but this is urgent. Can you confirm whether our reserved capacity is being honoured and what immediate mitigations you can apply? We need a short ETA for customer-impact remediation and any temporary fallback options.

I attached a zip of a few sample 5xx traces and a short screenshot of the dashboard.

—Lena

Lena, Carlos —

Thanks for flagging — I'm on it. Aditya and Ben, looping you in for immediate triage (see attached sample traces).

Initial notes from the monitoring surface: reserved throughput for EntangleFin's pool is saturated and the shared GPU cluster is showing queuing for KV cache writes. We're seeing a mix of long-generation burst patterns from a few high-QPS customers plus some tail behaviour causing token backpressure.

Immediate asks:
- Aditya / Ben: can you confirm whether the reservation controller is honoring the committed tokens or if there's a routing fallback happening?
- Ops: please propose a 4-hour mitigation (burst capacity or reroute to an overflow pool) and an estimate for customer-visible improvement.
- Carlos/Lena: If you have any recent traffic pattern changes (new model, longer prompts) please share.

I'll escalate to leadership if we need emergency burst approval. We'll keep this thread as the single source of truth.

—Marcus

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-19T09:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx surge — reserved capacity not delivering

Quick technical triage (short):
- Root signal: Dedicated GPU pool for EntangleFin is fully utilized; reservation controller shows committed qps being consumed but backpressure is coming from an unexpected increase in long-sequence generations (median sequence length +2.3x over baseline for the last 40m).
- Side effect: When pool is saturated, the smart router is degrading to best-effort variants for non-critical traffic; however some requests (authorized by the reservation token) are still queuing rather than immediately failing, producing 5xx timeouts downstream.

Immediate mitigations I've initiated (non-disruptive):
1) Enabled aggressive prefix caching for EntangleFin (should reduce token work on repeated prompts) — rolling now.
2) Prepared a temporary fallback plan: route low-priority endpoints to a compatible 8-bit quantized variant (faster exec path) — needs approval for cross-tenant burst.
3) Raised a hot ops job to temporarily expand the dedicated pool by +25% capacity via burst GPUs (4 hours). Requires exec sign-off for overage/credits.

Attached: emergency_runbook.md (contains exact ops steps and rollback). Estimated customer p95 reduction: 30–45% within 15 minutes of burst activation; 5xxs to fall to <0.5% if cache and routing take effect.

I recommend immediate executive approval to start the +4h burst while we continue to tune model routing.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: emergency_runbook.md]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-19T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx surge — reserved capacity not delivering

Marcus / Aditya —

Ops status: we've validated the reservation controller is not dropping committed tokens, but overall headroom for EntangleFin's dedicated pool is at ~97%. There's insufficient spare capacity to absorb this burst via internal scheduling. Aditya's cache/routing changes are in flight.

Impact and ask:
- Risk: If we do not authorize burst capacity now, EntangleFin faces an SLA breach with measurable customer transaction failures.
- Request: Approve emergency burst: +4 GPUs for 4 hours (estimated cost impact: ~$9k) and temporarily permit routing to a compatible quantized variant for non-critical endpoints (no model changes to customer code).

If leadership approves, Ops will activate at T+10m and run the changes in Aditya's runbook. We'll monitor p95 and 5xxs and report every 10 minutes to this thread.

—Ben
